# Dimension 1 — Setup and installation

What it takes to get Codex CLI installed, authenticated and configured, and
where each of those things lives on disk. Source details in
[citations](../citations.md).

Everything below was fetched 2026-08-21. No OpenAI documentation page states a
publication date, so "current" means "as served on that date".

## Install paths

| Method | Exact command | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Standalone (macOS/Linux) | `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh \| sh` | [37] |
| Standalone (Windows) | `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 \| iex"` | [37] |
| npm | `npm install -g @openai/codex` | [37] |
| Homebrew | `brew install --cask codex` | [37] |
| Direct binary | GitHub Release artifacts, e.g. `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | [37] |

The install command and the update command are the same string [36]. Installers
"download from `https://releases.openai.com/codex` by default and fall back to
GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable"; force GitHub
Releases with `CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false` [37].

**No container install path is documented.** The repository's install listing
names macOS/Linux, Windows, npm and Homebrew only [36][37]. A `.devcontainer`
exists in the repo [47] but it is a development environment for the Codex Rust
source, not a distribution channel. **No winget package appears in any fetched
page** — this is an argument from two install-listing pages, not proof of
absence.

The statically-linked musl artifact is the relevant one for a container:
`codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`, whose single entry must be renamed to
`codex` after extraction [37].

**Version anchor.** The changelog's newest dated entry as fetched is **Codex CLI
0.149.0, 2026-08-20**, with `npm install -g @openai/codex@0.149.0`; preceding
entries are 0.148.0 (2026-08-18) and 0.147.0 (2026-08-07) [6]. Git tags carry a
`rust-v` prefix (`rust-v0.149.0`) [6]. The `v0.143.0` string on the CLI landing
page appears inside a terminal mockup and is not a normative current-version
claim [8].

## Authentication

Two modes, and the choice has consequences beyond billing [4]:

> "When you sign in with ChatGPT, Codex usage follows your ChatGPT workspace
> permissions, role-based access control (RBAC), and ChatGPT Enterprise
> retention and residency settings. With an API key, usage follows your API
> organization's retention and data-sharing settings instead." [4]

> "When you sign in with an API key, Codex uses standard API pricing instead of
> included ChatGPT plan credits." [4]

> "The ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI, and IDE extension support both sign-in
> methods for local work. **Codex cloud requires signing in with ChatGPT.**" [4]

| Purpose | Command | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Browser sign-in (default) | `codex login` | [4] |
| Device-code sign-in (beta) | `codex login --device-auth` | [4] |
| API key, non-interactive | `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY \| codex login --with-api-key` | [4] |
| Enterprise access token | `printenv CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN \| codex login --with-access-token` | [4] |
| Check mode | `codex login status` | [4] |
| Clear | `codex logout` | [4] |

Credentials cache at **`~/.codex/auth.json`** — "a plaintext file" — or in the
OS credential store, selected by
`cli_auth_credentials_store = "file" | "keyring" | "auto"` [4]. The CLI and the
IDE extension share the same cache; logging out of either invalidates both [4].

Device-code login is **administratively gateable**: "Enable device code login in
your ChatGPT security settings (personal account) or ChatGPT workspace
permissions (workspace admin)" [4]. Issue #9253 (opened 2026-01-15, Codex
0.84.0) reports the failure mode when it is disabled — the exact error is
`"Please contact your workspace admin to enable device code authentication"`
[40]. That issue shows as Closed with no comments, no linked PR and no close
date, so closure cannot be read as a fix [40].

**Open question the docs do not settle:** whether the CLI reads `OPENAI_API_KEY`
ambiently for the built-in `openai` provider, or only via the documented pipe
into `codex login --with-api-key`. Every documented usage is the pipe form [4],
and `OPENAI_API_KEY` is **not** in the published environment-variable list [15].
`env_key` is documented only for custom providers [1].

## Config file locations and precedence

> "Codex stores user-level configuration at `~/.codex/config.toml`. To scope
> settings to a specific project or subfolder, add a `.codex/config.toml` file
> in your repo." [2]

Resolution order, highest precedence first [2]:

1. CLI flags and `--config` overrides
2. Project config files: `.codex/config.toml`, project root down to CWD, closest
   wins — **trusted projects only**
3. Profile files selected with `--profile <name>` (`~/.codex/<name>.config.toml`)
4. User config `~/.codex/config.toml`
5. System config `/etc/codex/config.toml` on Unix
6. Built-in defaults

Codex state lives under `CODEX_HOME` (default `~/.codex`): `config.toml`,
`auth.json`, `history.jsonl`, logs and caches [3][15]. If `CODEX_HOME` is set,
"the directory must already exist" [15].

### Ten keys that are ignored at project scope

> "Codex ignores `openai_base_url`, `chatgpt_base_url`, `apps_mcp_product_sku`,
> `model_provider`, `model_providers`, `notify`, `profile`, `profiles`,
> `experimental_realtime_ws_base_url`, and `otel` when they appear in a
> project-local `.codex/config.toml`; put provider, notification, and telemetry
> keys in user-level config instead." [1]

The advanced page adds that Codex "prints a startup warning when it sees them"
[3]. This matters directly for a sandbox that uploads config from a host: any
provider or telemetry routing must be written into the **user-level** file, not
a project file.

### Trust gate

> "If you mark a project as untrusted, Codex skips project-scoped `.codex/`
> layers, including project-local config, hooks, and rules. User and system
> config still load, including user/global hooks and rules." [2]

Trust is recorded in the *global* file as
`projects.<path>.trust_level = "trusted" | "untrusted"` [1].

### Profiles — a breaking change worth knowing

> "In **Codex 0.134.0 and later**, `--profile` no longer reads
> `[profiles.profile-name]` from `config.toml`, and the top-level
> `profile = "profile-name"` selector is no longer supported. Move legacy
> profile settings into `~/.codex/profile-name.config.toml`…" [3]

Profile names accept letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores [3].

### `requirements.toml`

Admin-enforced constraints users cannot override, with allowlists including
`allowed_approval_policies`, `allowed_sandbox_modes`,
`allowed_permission_profiles`, `allowed_web_search_modes`, and an `mcp_servers`
allowlist where "Both the server name (`<id>`) and its identity must match" [1].
`allow_managed_hooks_only = true` is supported **only** here, not in
`config.toml` [48].

**Gap:** none of the fetched pages states where `requirements.toml` lives on
disk. The config reference defers to an "Admin-enforced requirements" page that
was not fetched [1].

## `AGENTS.md` discovery

Codex builds its instruction chain once per run (once per TUI session), in this
order [5]:

- **Global scope** — in `CODEX_HOME` (default `~/.codex`): `AGENTS.override.md`
  if present, otherwise `AGENTS.md`. First non-empty file only.
- **Project scope** — from the project root (typically the Git root) down to
  CWD. In each directory: `AGENTS.override.md`, then `AGENTS.md`, then any
  `project_doc_fallback_filenames`. **At most one file per directory.**
- **Merge** — concatenated root-down, joined with blank lines; closer files
  override earlier ones by appearing later in the combined prompt.

> "Codex skips empty files and stops adding files once the combined size reaches
> the limit defined by `project_doc_max_bytes` (**32 KiB by default**)." [5]

> "Filenames not on this list are ignored for instruction discovery." [5]

Project root detection is `project_root_markers`, defaulting to a directory
containing `.git`; `project_root_markers = []` disables the parent search [3].

**Unresolved inconsistency between OpenAI's own pages:** the AGENTS.md guide
says `project_doc_max_bytes` caps the *combined* size [5], while the config
reference describes it as "Maximum bytes read from AGENTS.md" [1] and the
advanced page as "how much to read from **each** `AGENTS.md` file" [3]. The
32 KiB default is stated only in the guide.

Two keys can bypass AGENTS.md entirely: `model_instructions_file`
("Replacement for built-in instructions instead of AGENTS.md") and
`developer_instructions` [1]. `instructions` is "Reserved for future use" [1].

Auditing which files loaded: `codex -c log_dir=./.codex-log` then read
`./.codex-log/codex-tui.log` [5].

## MCP server configuration

Stored in `config.toml` — `~/.codex/config.toml` by default, or a project
`.codex/config.toml` for trusted projects [13].

Two transports, distinguished by which key is set [1][13]:

- **stdio** — `command` (required), plus `args`, `env`, `env_vars`, `cwd`
- **Streamable HTTP** — `url` (required), plus `http_headers`,
  `env_http_headers`, `bearer_token_env_var`, `auth`, `scopes`

CLI: `codex mcp add <server-name> --env VAR1=VALUE1 -- <stdio server-command>`,
e.g. `codex mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp` [13]. Also
`codex mcp list`, `codex mcp login <name>`, `codex mcp logout <name>`,
`codex mcp remove <name>`; `/mcp` in the TUI [13].

Shared keys and their defaults: `startup_timeout_sec` **10**, `tool_timeout_sec`
**60**, plus `enabled`, `required`, `enabled_tools`, `disabled_tools` (applied
*after* `enabled_tools`), `default_tools_approval_mode`
(`auto | prompt | writes | approve`) [13].

`required = true` makes `codex exec` exit with an error if that server fails to
initialize, rather than continuing without it [23].
